newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen end lower on BOJ's morning operation.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen end lower on BOJ's morning operation.

text.p: The key December three-month euroyen futures contract ended lower on Thursday.
Traders said the Bank of Japan's decision to scale back the fund surplus in the money market from the previous day's level, caught the market by surprise, and led to selling of euroyen futures.
The BOJ drained 500 billion yen from the money market through its regular money market operation this morning.
The operation left the money market with a fund surplus of about 70 billion yen.
On Wednesday, the BOJ had left a fund surplus of about 300 billion yen in the money market.
The key overnight call rate rose to 0.52 percent due to the BOJ operation, up from Wednesday's weighted average of 0.45 percent, traders said.
The fact that the key overnight call rate rose despite the central bank's decision to maintain an accommodative stance shows that short-end fund demand is strong, traders said.

The BOJ will probably leave a fund surplus of about 100 billion yen through its operation on Friday since the overnight call rate is unlikely to rise too much ahead of the weekend, a trader for a long-term credit bank said.
The key December three-month euroyen futures were sold early this morning on an announcement by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd that it and Bankers Trust New York Corp had agreed on a business alliance.
"The news fueled speculation (in the morning) that Tokyo share prices would rise, and led to selling of euroyen futures," a city bank trader said.
The BOJ's operation intensified the selling and triggered long liquidation, traders said.

The December was lifted off lows in the afternoon as Tokyo share prices ended sharply lower, and as the key June 10-year Japanese government bond futures pared earlier losses to end slightly higher, they said.
February machinery orders data, released in the afternoon had little effect on the market, traders said.
"Machinery orders came in a bit stronger than expected, but it had little impact. There is not much interest in economic data for February," another city bank trader said.
Japan's private-sector machinery orders fell a seasonally adjusted 1.6 percent in February from the previous month, the Economic Planning Agency said on Thursday.

Interest rate swap (IRS) rates were little changed from the previous day's levels by late afternoon, a trust bank trader said. Market players seem eager to receive fixed interest rates when rates rise, preventing a sharp rise in rates, he said.
About 170 billion yen worth of key three-month certificates of deposit were issued at 0.55 percent. About 50 billion yen worth of two-month CDs were issued at 0.54 percent.
